sources.title: Structured interview note preserving all-courses SQL wording

claims.text: Strongest repository source preserves only the task of returning student names whose every course score is not below 60; schema names, zero-course semantics, NULL handling, retakes, and ordering are not source-proven.

Under the explicitly declared non-null one-row-per-student-course schema and zero-course exclusion contract, grouping by student and requiring MIN(score) >= 60 returns exactly students whose recorded course scores are all at least 60.

validation.command: extract main candidate SQL; execute against independent in-memory SQLite oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS included=Alice,Cara,Eve,Gina exact60=included any-below60=excluded single-course-pass=included zero-course=excluded repeated60=included

boundary_tests.case: one score below 60 among higher scores

boundary_tests.expected: student excluded by declared INNER JOIN contract

findings: Repository source preserves only the SQL goal of returning student names whose every course score is not below 60; schema names, zero-course semantics, NULL handling, retakes, and ordering are not source-proven.
Candidate labels its students/scores schema, non-null one-row-per-course assumption, and zero-course exclusion as explicit reference-contract choices rather than source facts.

Under a non-empty non-null score set, MIN(score) >= 60 is equivalent to the universal condition that every recorded score is at least 60; the answer also gives the equivalent EXISTS plus NOT EXISTS form.
Independent SQLite oracle passes exact-60 inclusion, any-sub-60 rejection, single-course pass, zero-course exclusion, and repeated boundary-value courses.
Answer identifies same-name grouping, NULL, retake, empty-set, ordering, and index/explain boundaries without fabricating production experience.
